title: onboarding-fidelity-accelerator-prd-commercialization-path-2026-04-14
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview

Purpose
This PRD describes the Onboarding Fidelity Accelerator (OFA): a productized toolkit and backend service that accelerates new-customer time-to-value by recommending fidelity profiles, issuing onboarding credit packages, and providing a lightweight simulation of production cost/SLO tradeoffs for early usage. OFA is intended to reduce churn during the first 30 days, lower average onboarding TCO, and create a repeatable commercialization funnel for fidelity-addons.

Background and problem statement
- Customers frequently struggle to pick the correct fidelity (model variant, quantization, batching profile) when they try Redwood for the first time. Incorrect choices lead to high early cost, slow latency, or poor quality, and many proof-of-concepts stall.
- Sales and success teams manually advise accounts; there is no standardized product surface that encodes common heuristics, early-credit offers, or a fast simulation experience for customers to preview economics.

Goals (30/60/90)
1) 30 days: Ship the OFA backend and UI card in Console to collect three signals (intent, latency preference, budget) and return a recommended fidelity profile. Provide an automated 2-week onboarding credit voucher generator.
2) 60 days: Add a developer simulation sandbox (offline traffic simulator) that runs a 5-minute synthetic workload and reports expected cost and latency ranges with toggles for batching and KV caching.
3) 90 days: Enable a commercial workflow that maps recommended fidelity into purchasable add-ons (e.g., fidelity-boost credits, warm-capacity coupons) and A/B tests the conversion uplift versus a control cohort.

Non-goals
- OFA will not replace the full Optimize product in scope or features (no advanced multi-tenant billing or long-term fidelity autoscaling in MVE).
- OFA will not perform live customer model re-training or change customer model weights.

Success metrics
- 30-day onboarding retention rate for OFA-enabled accounts vs control: +12% relative improvement.
- Average first-month inference unit cost for new customers: -18% (by volume-weighted average).
- Conversion rate to paid fidelity-addons within 60 days for OFA recommendations: >= 6%.
- Simulation accuracy: predicted cost within +/- 15% of real measured cost for 70% of sampled accounts after 30 days.

User personas and primary flows
- Developer (self-serve): Discovers OFA card in Console onboarding flow, answers 3 quick questions, runs a 5-minute simulation, accepts recommended profile and auto-applies a voucher.
- Platform Engineer (enterprise): Reviews recommended fidelity in the Console, requests tailored onboarding credit via Sales, and receives an SLA-informed fidelity mapping for Dedicated capacity.
- Solutions/Success Engineer: Runs a guided experiment for customers, exports sim results, and seeds a trial fidelity profile into the customer's tenant.

Functional requirements
- FR-1: Console UI card capturing intent, expected throughput (RPS), latency SLO, and cost sensitivity flag (low/medium/high).
- FR-2: Backend recommendation engine that returns: model_variant, quantization_profile, batching_profile, cache_policy, expected_cost_range, expected_latency_range. Recommendations must be deterministic for identical inputs.
- FR-3: Offline simulator that accepts a short trace (synthetic or user-uploaded) and runs a performance/cost estimator producing a CSV and console report.
- FR-4: Voucher generator that issues time-limited onboarding credits tied to tenant ID and limits (max credit $X, expiration 14 days).
- FR-5: Event telemetry and analytics signals for AB test cohorts: saw_recommendation, ran_simulation, accepted_profile, redeemed_voucher, conversion_to_paid_addon.

Non-functional requirements
- NFR-1: Recommendation latency <= 300ms for interactive Console calls.
- NFR-2: Simulator run time <= 5 minutes for synthetic 10k-token workload; resource usage to be rate-limited per tenant.
- NFR-3: Data residency: simulator traces and recommendation inputs must obey tenant data-residency settings (no cross-region copy by default).
- NFR-4: Security: voucher issuance must require role=billing-admin or system-sales role. All issued vouchers logged to audit trail (audit-log event).

Design overview
- Components:
  - Console UI Card (FE): React component, new route '/onboarding/accelerator'.
  - Recommendation Service (BE): stateless API microservice exposing /recommend v1.0. Implements heuristics + lightweight rules engine.
  - Simulator Worker Pool: k8s job workers that run cost/latency estimations using model performance profiles from the Performance Catalog service.
  - Voucher Service (BE): integrates with billing to mint one-time coupons.

Recommendation heuristics (high level)
- Input signals: workload type (chat/generate/embedding), avg prompt length, desired latency percentile (p95 target), cost sensitivity.
- Heuristic rules examples:
  - If latency target <= 150ms and cost sensitivity != high => prefer small higher-fidelity variant or low-quant quantized 16-bit variant.
  - If cost sensitivity == high and prompt length < 64 tokens => prefer quantized 8-bit variant + aggressive batching profile.
  - If session-based chat with KV cacheable content => recommend cache_policy: prefix_kv_enabled and suggest session length cap for affordable cost.

API contract (example)
POST /v1/onboarding/recommend
Request body (JSON):
{
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "workload": "chat|generate|embedding",
  "avg_prompt_tokens": 120,
  "target_latency_p95_ms": 250,
  "cost_sensitivity": "low|medium|high"
}
Response (JSON):
{
  "model_variant": "mix-6b-int8",
  "quantization_profile": "int8-q4_0",
  "batching_profile": "auto:64ms-max-100",
  "cache_policy": "prefix_kv:enabled",
  "expected_cost_cents_per_1k_tokens": "45-72",
  "expected_latency_p95_ms": "140-220",
  "confidence": "0.78"
}

Pricing and packaging implications
- Commercial primitives: onboarding-credit (one-time), fidelity-add-on SKU (monthly or consumption based), simulation-run pack (metered).
- Proposed starter pricing matrix (for GTM/finance discussion):
| SKU | What it includes | Price to customer (USD) | Redwood margin note |
|-----|------------------|------------------------:|---------------------|
| onboarding-credit-100 | $100 refundable trial credits | $0 (promotional) | Costed against sales budget |
| fidelity-add-on-boost | Guaranteed p95 latency uplift SLA + priority routing | $500/mo | Premium add-on for enterprise |
| sim-run-10 | 10 simulation runs | $50 | Lower-cost experimentation bundle |

- Billing flow: vouchers reduce hosted usage first, then customers are converted to paid SKUs when credit used or expiration reached. Financial controls required to cap potential promotion cost exposure.

Launch plan and roadmap themes
- Phase 0 (Discovery, 2 weeks): Stakeholder interviews (Sales, Success, Finance), gather top 20 onboarding failure cases, baseline metrics.
- Phase 1 (MVP, 6 weeks): Implement FR-1/FR-2/FR-4 with Console card, simple voucher issuance, and telemetry. Limited beta with 25 self-serve orgs.
- Phase 2 (Beta expansion, 8 weeks): Add Simulator (FR-3), A/B test cohort mechanics and conversion tracking; integrate with Optimize telemetry to surface fidelity recommendations in Console.
- Phase 3 (Commercial launch, 4 weeks): Add pricing SKUs, integrate with billing catalog, sales enablement materials, and 1:many webinars.

Operational considerations and runbook excerpts
- Alerting:
  - Recommendation service 5xx rate > 1% over 5m -> pager (eng-oncall).
  - Simulator job queue latency > 10m for >95th percentile -> SRE on-call.
- Capacity planning:
  - Assume 1000 new tenants/month adoption ramp. Estimate simulator worker capacity: 250 parallel jobs to keep 95th latency under 5m.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Poor simulation accuracy could erode trust. Mitigation: conservative confidence score, surface historical prediction error, and require explicit user confirmation before applying profile.
- Risk: Voucher abuse and cost overruns. Mitigation: per-tenant caps, fraud detection, manual approval for >$500 vouchers.
- Risk: Sales ops complexity across Dedicated vs Hosted. Mitigation: shipping separate gating logic (tenant.type) and SRE playbook for Dedicated onboarding.

Appendix A — Configuration table (example defaults)
| Field | Default | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| max_voucher_amount_usd | 100 | Admin-configurable via billing console |
| simulator_timeout_seconds | 300 | Hard timeout enforced |
| recommendation_max_batch_ms | 64 | Upper bound for batching suggestion |

Appendix B — Example simulator CLI (for internal use)
```bash
# run a quick synthetic sim for tenant
redwood sim-run --tenant-id t-12345 --workload chat --rps 10 --duration 300 --out report.csv
```

Appendix C — Follow-up experiments (hypothesis-driven)
- Experiment 1: Auto-apply recommendations vs user-accept flow — measure conversion and satisfaction.
- Experiment 2: Different voucher sizes (50/100/250) to quantify marginal conversion uplift per $ spent.
